Theme 1 • Short Questions

Information, Crime, and Corruption

Phillips et al. (2022) • Dlodlo (2013) • Cyber Typologies

🎭 The Drama Hook

A burglar 8,000 miles away doesn't pick your lock; he injects 10 lines of malicious ransomware that paralyzes Durban's port logistics, causing R100 million in rotting cargo while demanding Bitcoin.

⚙️ The Academic Mechanism
  • Cyber-Dependent: Crimes that ONLY exist via ICT (Ransomware, DDoS, malware).
  • Cyber-Enabled: Traditional crimes amplified by ICT (Phishing fraud, identity theft).
  • SA Vulnerability: High mobile penetration + low cyber literacy + porous enforcement.
Cyber-Dependent Cyber-Enabled Ripple Effects Biometric SASSA
Theme 2 • 20M Essay Giant

Political Economy & The Malawi Case

Paul Sturges (1998) • Dr Hastings Banda (1964–1994) • Mark Graham

🎭 The Drama Hook

President Banda banned the song 'Cecilia' because his ex-lover had that name, banned the word "poverty" from newspapers, and jailed librarians with torn books. Controlling information was his instrument of state survival.

⚙️ The Academic Mechanism
  • Information Monopoly: The state controls media to suppress political pluralism.
  • Information Poverty: Citizens were deprived of agricultural and medical knowledge.
  • Geography of Info (Graham): Global North produces 80% of digital content; South is passive.
Censorship Board Information Poverty State Hegemony Graham Unevenness
Theme 3 • Short Questions

Microeconomics: Pricing Information Goods

Shapiro & Varian • Douglas Laney (Infonomics) • Metcalfe's Law

🎭 The Drama Hook

Spotify spends $100M coding its streaming app. But streaming copy #2 to your phone costs literally R0.00. Standard cost-plus pricing breaks! You must charge for value through versioning and bundling.

⚙️ The Academic Mechanism
  • Cost Structure: High fixed sunk costs ($FC$), near-zero marginal cost ($MC \approx 0$).
  • Non-Rivalrous: Multiple people consume without depleting it.
  • Pricing Weapons: Versioning (Free vs Premium), Bundling (Office 365), Lock-in.
MC ≈ 0 Non-Rivalrous Experience Good Versioning & Bundling
Theme 4 • Short Questions

Macroeconomics: The 5th Factor of Production

Machlup & Porat • Gender Macroeconomics • Leapfrogging

🎭 The Drama Hook

A gold mine with 5,000 workers goes bankrupt without geological data software. Information is no longer a footnote; it is the 5th Factor of Production multiplying land, labour, and capital.

⚙️ The Academic Mechanism
  • The 4+1 Factors: Land, Labour, Capital, Entrepreneurship + Information.
  • Industry Sectors: Primary (pure tech/telecom) vs Secondary (internal accounting/HR).
  • Gender Lens: Women in rural Africa disproportionately face data poverty and device exclusion.
5th Factor Primary vs Secondary Leapfrogging Gender Digital Divide
Theme 5 • 20M Essay Giant

Networked Readiness Index (NRI) & SA

Portulans Institute (2024/2025) • 4 Pillars • Section 16 & PAIA

🎭 The Drama Hook

Think of NRI as a smartphone: Technology is the hardware; People are the user; Governance is privacy settings; Impact is the apps improving your life. Having cables in the ground is useless if people cannot afford data.

⚙️ The Academic Mechanism
  • 4 Pillars (T-P-G-I): Technology, People, Governance, Impact.
  • SA Strengths: Top in Governance (POPIA, cyber laws, banking regulation).
  • SA Weaknesses: Severe digital skills deficit, load shedding, high data tariffs.
Technology People Governance Impact
Theme 6 • Short Questions

Trends in South African Info Industries

Informatisation • Digital Activism (#FeesMustFall) • Fintech

🎭 The Drama Hook

South Africa has dirt roads with zero running water where street vendors take instant QR code payments on mobile. High-tech informatisation thrives alongside stark structural inequality.

⚙️ The Academic Mechanism
  • Informatisation: Shift from mining/metals to data, software, and financial services.
  • Digital Activism: #FeesMustFall bypassed traditional broadcasters to mobilize nation.
  • Brain Drain: Local devs hired remotely by US/EU firms earning foreign currency.
Informatisation Fintech Leapfrog #FeesMustFall Remote Brain Drain
Theme 7 • 20M Essay Giant

Social Media vs. Social Networking

Tugtekin & Koc (2019) • 5 Structural Differences • CSR

🎭 The Drama Hook

Shouting through a megaphone into a crowd is Social Media (Broadcast). Walking into a dinner party and having deep 1-on-1 conversations is Social Networking (Relationships). Never confuse them!

⚙️ The Academic Mechanism
  • 5 Differences (B-M-V-N-C): Broadcast vs Relationship; 1-to-Many vs Many-to-Many; Virality vs Trust; Networks vs Channels; Content vs Social Capital.
  • CSR Communication: Media for broadcast (risking greenwashing); Networking for real dialogue.
Broadcast vs Relationship Asymmetric vs Symmetric Network Graph CSR Greenwashing
Theme 8 • 20M Essay Giant

Marketing Mix & 5 Company Orientations

Philip Kotler • John Jeyasekar (2020) • The 7Ps of Info Goods

🎭 The Drama Hook

An engineer builds the world's most complex search portal, but users run away because you need a PhD to type a search. This is Marketing Myopia: loving your code instead of solving human pain.

⚙️ The Academic Mechanism
  • 5 Concepts (P-P-S-M-S): Production, Product, Selling, Marketing, Societal Marketing.
  • The 7Ps of Services: Product, Price, Place, Promotion + People, Process, Physical Evidence.
Production Concept Marketing Myopia Societal Concept Extended 7Ps

Exemplar Essay 1: Paul Sturges & Political Economy of Malawi (1964–1994)

Question: Critically discuss how state control of information serves as an instrument of political power. [20 Marks]

🔍 The Examiner's Red Pen: 4/20 vs 18/20 Comparison (Click to Inspect) ▼
❌ Typical Failing Student (4/20):

"Banda was a dictator in Malawi and he banned lots of things like books and radio. People didn't know what was happening because the government lied. That's why information is bad when censored."

Marker notes: Zero citations (Sturges missing). No mention of political economy, information monopoly, Censorship Board, or information poverty.
✅ Distinction Student (18/20):

"According to Paul Sturges (1998), Dr. Hastings Banda's 30-year regime operated an information monopoly through the Censorship Board. Information control was not merely ideological; it was an instrument of state hegemony to enforce political compliance and engineer systemic information poverty..."

Marker notes: Immediate author citation, theoretical framework (state hegemony, monopoly), concrete mechanism (Censorship Board), and systemic outcome (information poverty).

📄 The 60-Second Scrap Paper Protocol

Exam Hall 1-Page Memory Dump

The second the invigilator says "You may begin", flip your rough paper over and write down these four acronyms before opening the paper. Mental blanking becomes impossible.

THEME 2 ESSAY Paul Sturges

Malawi Censorship: M - O - N - O

  • M — Monopoly of information by the state.
  • O — Oppression of dissent (Censorship Board).
  • N — National isolation & information poverty.
  • O — Overthrow of reality: info control = state survival.
THEME 5 ESSAY Portulans Institute

NRI 4 Pillars: T - P - G - I

  • T — Technology (Hardware, fiber, 5G, AI access).
  • P — People (Digital skills, business & gov usage).
  • G — Governance (Trust, privacy laws, POPIA, security).
  • I — Impact (Economic GDP, quality of life, SDGs).
SA Profile: High in Governance; weak in People (skills) and load shedding grid instability.
THEME 7 ESSAY Tugtekin & Koc

Media vs Networking: B - M - V - N - C

  • B — Broadcast vs Relationship.
  • M — Many-to-Many vs One-to-Many.
  • V — Virality vs Trust/Community.
  • N — Networks vs Content Channels.
  • C — Content vs Social Capital.
THEME 8 ESSAY Philip Kotler

Marketing Concepts: P - P - S - M - S

  • P — Production: Low cost, mass availability.
  • P — Product: High features (Marketing Myopia risk).
  • S — Selling: Aggressive hard-sell pitches.
  • M — Marketing: Customer-centric satisfaction.
  • S — Societal: Long-term ethics, privacy, public good.
7Ps for Services: Product, Price, Place, Promotion + People, Process, Physical Evidence.
